record_type_quote: In two pre-registered studies, we conducted a replication and extension of three classic experiments on past behaviour exception/routine contrasts (N = 684).

targets.title: Norm theory: Comparing reality to its alternatives.
targets.evidence_quote: Parts 1 and 2 of this replication use the classic hitch-hiker and car-accident scenarios from Kahneman and Miller (1986).
targets.outcome_quote: The hitchhiker and car accident scenarios (Kahneman & Miller, 1986) were fully replicated.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly judge both original scenarios fully replicated across the two new-sample experiments. Original scenarios are not assigned numbered studies in the text.

targets.title: Counterfactual thinking and victim compensation: A test of norm theory.
targets.evidence_quote: Part 3 is a replication of Experiment 1 from Miller and McFarland (1986) with the robbery-scenario – the study that meant to provide the ﬁrst empirical test of norm theory.
targets.outcome_quote: The robbery scenario (Miller & McFarland, 1986) failed to replicate using the original experimental paradigm using a compensation measure, yet we found support for an exceptionality eﬀect using an added measure of perceived regret.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit failure verdict on original compensation finding. Positive perceived-regret finding is an added extension and does not confirm the original compensation result.

reasoning: Two new experiments each include three scenario parts drawn from two original papers. Both original papers are coded once; extensions motivated by other works do not themselves directly re-test those papers. Saved main article includes cover and journal pages 901–914; appended supplement is excluded.
